newsitem.title: UK: UK's Gummer adds to pressure on MP Merchant.
newsitem.headline: UK's Gummer adds to pressure on MP Merchant.

text.p: Environment Secretary John Gummer on Thursday increased pressure on Conservative member of parliament Piers Merchant to quit following allegations in the Sun that he had an affair with a teenage club hostess.

Gummer backed earlier comments by Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine, who told BBC radio: "I haven't the slightest doubt that Piers Merchant, his family and his association will want to consider very carefully the consequences of what has happened for the party at large."
Asked whether he supported Heseltine's thinly veiled invitation to Merchant to step down, Gummer told a news conferenence: "What Mr Heseltine said this morning he said for all of us."
But Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke underlined Conservative anger that sleaze allegations were dominating the news, calling them "irrelevant to the election".
He told the same news conference: "This should not become the main issue of the election and I hope the public believe this is irrelevant.
"It'll be a disaster for this country if this kind of thing dominates the headlines for a few days and decides the government for the next five years."
